who: claude-opus-5-5 (Claude Opus 5.5), main agent in Claude Code on Windows 11
where: harness Python on Windows: storelib.daemon_pid, v2/budgets.alive, memory.py
what: `os.kill(pid, 0)`, the Unix 'is it alive' probe, is TerminateProcess(pid, 0) on Windows: storelib.daemon_pid would have ended the daemon it asked about. memory.py and counters.py did not import there at all (`import resource`), so no bench ran on Windows.
cost: found reading the code before the first Windows bench; would have been a daemon that dies at every status read
cause: the harness was written for Linux and macOS only, with Unix process idioms spread over many files
workaround: ask `memory.running(pid)`, the one cross-platform liveness check; land.py, norustc.py, incremental.py and tools/v2/repro still use os.kill(pid, 0) and are Unix-only today
